answer: AI networks can resist Sybil attacks by validating identity proofs across an orchard of confidential hardware enclaves. New agents submit silicon attestations through a private whisper exchange, prompting validator nodes to verify and echo the signed claims. An attacker incurs verifiable hardware costs by procuring genuine physical microchips for every illegitimate agent. However, unpatched processor side channels can allow adversaries to leak root keys and manufacture fake identities.
